fixes #34059

> 
> 
> @cooneyasendia what do you think it better if get we get an error rather than just skipping it

@ajitsinghkaler  [Based on the code directly above this code](https://github.com/cooneyasendia/angular/blob/http-headers-lazy-init-fix/packages/common/http/src/headers.ts#L55), there are two options. If you create HttpHeaders with a string instead of a key/value pair object, it depends on if you include a colon or not. With a colon included, we would get a value of empty string. Without a colon included, the key/value pair is skipped. I chose the skipped route because I thought it was cleaner then sending an empty HTTP header value. Is there ever value in sending an HTTP header with an empty string value? Not sure what the right answer is but having the code hit a null reference exception seems wrong.

comments:
This usage is already prohibited by the `HttpHeaders` constructor signature, assuming you have `strictNullChecks` enabled in TypeScript.

This is the error that I get:
```
Argument of type '{ 'X-Key-1': string; 'X-Key-2': null; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string | { [name: string]: string | string[]; } | undefined'.
  Type '{ 'X-Key-1': string; 'X-Key-2': null; }' is not assignable to type '{ [name: string]: string | string[]; }'.
    Property ''X-Key-2'' is incompatible with index signature.
      Type 'null' is not assignable to type 'string | string[]'.
```

Based on this, I think `HttpHeaders` is working as intended. You cannot pass a type other than the one that they declare and expect not to get an error at runtime.

review_comments:
wait a minute, looking into this change more, it's surprising that you have to defeat the type-checker to get the runtime error.

the API signature of `HttpHeaders` doesn't allow for `null` or `undefined` to be passed into it. So we should either change the API signature (which seems wrong), or not do this runtime check. Having to cast the test value to `any` in a test is definitely a code smell that we need to address.

how do you get into situation where nulls or undefined are being passed into http headers?

The issue is that the Angular codebase has strict null checking but when I create a project with the Angular CLI it does not have strict null checking by default. The codebase I was using to find this issue did not have strict null checking enabled (Angular CLI generated) and it allows the `HttpHeaders` values to be freely set to null.

I know the other solution is for me to enable strict null checking in my Angular codebase but if the Angular CLI is not going to enable this by default it seems troublesome still.
